easy.def: A word you say to mean not yes.
examples: No, I do not want any.
No, thank you.
No, it is not time yet.

more.def: A word used to give a negative answer, to refuse, or to say that something is not true.
examples: No, I have not finished my homework yet.
The sign said no, so we did not go in.
No, a spider is not an insect.
I have no pencil.
There is no milk left.
No one is home.

more.def: Not any, or not even one.
examples: There were no clouds in the sky all day.
The new puppy has no idea how to sit yet.
We had no school because of the snowstorm.
The noble knight helped the poor.
It was a noble act.
He is a noble man.

more.def: Showing high honor and goodness.
examples: The noble ruler gave food to the hungry.
It was a noble thing to share your lunch.
The noble dog saved its owner.

easy.def: A person of high rank in old times.
examples: The noble lived in a castle.
The nobles met with the king.
The nobles wore fine clothes.

more.def: A person of high rank in the past, such as a lord or lady.
examples: The noble lived in a castle on the hill.
The king invited the nobles to dinner.
In the story, a noble wore fine robes.
Nobody is home.
Nobody came.
Nobody knows.

more.def: No person at all.
examples: Nobody was in the classroom when I got there.
Nobody knew the answer, so the teacher explained it.
The room was so quiet that nobody made a sound.

easy.def: Awake at night and asleep in the day.
examples: Owls are nocturnal.
Bats are nocturnal.
A nocturnal animal sleeps in the day.

more.def: Active at night and resting during the day.
examples: Bats are nocturnal animals that hunt insects after dark.
The zoo has a dark room for nocturnal animals.
Raccoons are nocturnal and often visit at night.

easy.def: A sound, especially a loud one.
examples: The noise woke me.
The noise is loud.
I heard a funny noise.

more.def: A sound, especially one that is loud or not nice to hear.
examples: The noise from the road woke me.
I heard a funny noise in the attic.
The children made a lot of noise.
The noisy truck woke me up.
The noisy birds woke me up.
My baby brother is noisy.

more.def: Making a lot of loud sound, or full of loud sounds.
examples: The lunchroom is always noisy at noon.
The noisy fan kept me awake.
We moved away from the noisy road.
None of the cookies are left.
None of us knew.
I have none.

more.def: Not one, or not any.
examples: None of the students forgot their homework.
I looked for pencils, but there were none.
None of the cookies were left after the party.

easy.def: Silly words or ideas that mean nothing.
examples: That funny poem is full of nonsense.
Stop that nonsense and eat.
The baby talks nonsense.

more.def: Words or ideas that are silly or have no meaning.
examples: He made us laugh by singing a song of pure nonsense.
The idea that the moon is made of cheese is nonsense.
The writer filled his book with funny nonsense words.
We eat lunch at noon.
The sun is high at noon.
The bell rings at noon.

more.def: Twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.
examples: The shadows are shortest at noon.
The sun is highest in the sky at noon.
The school bell rang at noon.

easy.def: Used after "neither" to add a second thing.
examples: Neither Sam nor Mia came.
It is neither hot nor cold.
I like neither tea nor milk.

more.def: Used after "neither" or a negative word to add another thing that is also not true.
examples: Neither Sam nor Mia came to the party.
He did not call, nor did he write.
It was neither hot nor cold.
It is a normal school day.
A cold winter is normal here.
His temperature is normal.

more.def: Usual, ordinary and what you would expect.
examples: Rain is normal in the spring.
It was a normal day until the power went out.
Her temperature was normal.
I normally eat at six.
She normally walks to school.
It normally snows in winter.

more.def: In the usual way, or most of the time.
examples: I normally eat dinner at six.
She normally rides the bus to school.
It normally snows here in January.
Geese fly north in spring.
Polar bears live in the far north.
It is colder in the north.

more.def: The direction that is opposite to south, toward the top of most maps.
examples: A compass needle points north.
Many birds fly north in the spring.
Snow arrives early in the north.

easy.def: Having to do with the north.
examples: The northern sky is dark.
The northern part is cold.
Northern lights glow.

more.def: Found in, from or toward the north.
examples: The northern part of the state gets a lot of snow.
The northern lights glowed in the sky.
A cold northern wind blew.

easy.def: The part of your face you smell with.
examples: My nose is cold.
A dog has a wet nose.
He wiped his nose.

more.def: The part of the face above the mouth that is used for smelling and breathing.
examples: Dogs sniff with their wet noses.
She held her nose when she dove in the pool.
The clown wore a big red nose.

easy.def: A word that makes a word mean the other way.
examples: I am not sad.
The soup is not hot.
He did not come.

more.def: A word used to say that something is false or fails to happen, or to turn a word into its opposite.
examples: Penguins can swim, but they cannot fly, and that is not a mistake.
Please do not run in the hallway.
The test was not as hard as I thought.
I left a note for Mom.
She read the note.
There is a note on the fridge.

more.def: A short written message.
examples: I left a note for my mom on the fridge.
The teacher sent a note home.
She slipped a note under the door.
Play a note on the piano.
That note is high.
The bird sang a note.

more.def: A single sound of music, or the sign that shows it.
examples: She played one note on the piano.
The bird sang a high note.
The song starts on a low note.

easy.def: A book of paper for writing.
examples: I write in my notebook.
The notebook is blue.
I lost my notebook.

more.def: A book with blank pages that you use to write notes in.
examples: I wrote in my notebook during class.
The notebook has lined pages.
She keeps her ideas in a small notebook.
There is nothing in the box.
I have nothing to eat.
She said nothing.

more.def: Not anything, or no thing at all.
examples: There was nothing left in the bowl except a few crumbs.
He did nothing wrong, so he was not in trouble.
Nothing is faster than light.
Did you notice my new haircut?
I noticed a bug on the wall.
Mom noticed my clean room.

more.def: To become aware of something by seeing, hearing, or feeling it.
examples: He noticed a small crack in the window.
Nobody noticed that the door was open.
I noticed that the days are getting shorter.
The school will notify us.
I notified the teacher.
They notified the neighbors.

more.def: To tell someone officially about something.
examples: The school will notify parents about the snow day.
I notified my teacher that I would be late.
The firefighters notified the neighbors.

easy.def: A long story in a book.
examples: I read a novel.
The novel is long.
The novel has many chapters.

more.def: A long book of made-up stories about people and events.
examples: I read a novel about a boy and a dog.
The novel had twenty chapters.
She wrote a novel about space.
That is a novel idea.
The novel toy is new.
He had a novel way.

more.def: New, and not like anything before.
examples: That is a novel way to solve the puzzle.
The inventor had a novel idea for a machine.
The art teacher tried a novel way to paint.

easy.def: The eleventh month of the year.
examples: Thanksgiving is in November.
November has thirty days.
My birthday is in November.

more.def: The eleventh month of the year, after October and before December.
examples: Thanksgiving is celebrated in November.
Many families travel to see relatives in November.
The leaves are gone by November.
I am eating now.
Please come now.
It is snowing now.

more.def: At this moment, or very soon.
examples: The movie is starting now, so please be quiet.
I used to be afraid of the dark, but now I am not.
We must leave now if we want to catch the train.
Nowadays, we use phones.
Nowadays, people use computers.
Nowadays, it is easy to travel.

more.def: At the present time, as different from the past.
examples: Nowadays, most people have a phone.
Nowadays, we travel by car and plane.
Nowadays, kids use computers in school.
The cat is nowhere to be found.
I went nowhere.
There is nowhere to sit.

more.def: Not in or to any place.
examples: The keys were nowhere to be found.
There is nowhere to hide in the open field.
We had nowhere to go during the storm.
